title: Nuclear thermal propulsion fuel-element corrosion in hot hydrogen flow
bottleneck: Nuclear thermal rockets heat hydrogen propellant by flowing it directly through a uranium reactor core, roughly doubling chemical-rocket efficiency and potentially halving Mars transit times. But the superheated, corrosive hydrogen erodes and cracks the fuel elements: during the 1955-1973 NERVA program, fuel-element erosion was a recurring failure engineers never fully resolved. No fuel form has yet been proven to survive repeated high-temperature hydrogen exposure under flight conditions.
why_it_blocks: Without durable fuel elements, NTP engines cannot deliver the burn durations and restart cycles a crewed Mars mission requires, so the fastest near-term path to short interplanetary transits stays grounded.
current_state: BWXT is developing HALEU-based coated-particle fuel for the NASA-DARPA DRACO demonstration, and General Atomics reports fuel surviving simulated operating conditions in ground tests. A flight demo is targeted for 2027, but in-space performance remains unproven.
